definition: Share of price records that parse and carry every required field (code, code type, rate, rate type, billing class, expiration date)
why: A record that cannot be parsed or lacks a required field cannot be priced or compared at all

definition: Share of price rows whose service maps to a standard procedure code: billing_code is CPT/HCPCS/MS-DRG, or a revenue-code row carries a CPT/HCPCS-shaped code in additional_information
why: A revenue code alone (e.g. RC 636 'drugs') cannot be compared across payers; rates must be tied to a specific procedure to be benchmarked

definition: Share of rate rows whose provider reference resolves to an NPI
why: A rate that cannot be tied to a provider is unusable for provider-level benchmarking

definition: Share of benchmark codes (HiLabs Spec-Proc list) with at least one usable rate in the scored billing classes (default: professional), weighted by the codes' benchmark weight
why: A file is only useful for benchmarking if it prices the codes that drive spend; weighting stops a file scoring well on rare codes

definition: Share of benchmark (specialty, code) weight where a provider of that specialty (NPPES taxonomy -> HiLabs crosswalk) has a usable rate for that code
why: Contracting teams compare like with like: a cardiology code priced only for non-cardiologists does not support a cardiology benchmark

definition: Share of distinct NPIs that pass the check digit, exist in NPPES, are not deactivated and practise in the target state (NPPES primary or secondary address, or CMS DAC)
why: Invalid, retired or out-of-state providers inflate the network and point rates at people a CA contracting team cannot use

definition: Share of rate rows that are null, <= $0 or a known placeholder value
why: $0 and placeholder rates are not real prices and drag averages down; tolerance 10% (score 0 at 10% bad)

definition: Share of positive rates more than outlier_fold x above or below the median of their (code type, code, procedure code, service name, billing class, rate type) group (groups with >= outlier_min_group rates)
why: Order-of-magnitude deviations usually mean unit errors (cents vs dollars, per-unit vs per-case) or misattributed codes; tolerance 5%

definition: Share of rate rows whose negotiated_type converts directly to dollars (negotiated, fee schedule, derived)
why: Percentage-of-charges and per-diem rates cannot be compared as dollar amounts without a base that the file does not provide

definition: Share of rate rows that repeat another row on every business field (provider, code, context, type, rate, expiration)
why: Exact duplicates inflate counts and storage but do not change prices, so they are tolerated up to 50%

definition: Share of (NPI, TIN, code, modifier, billing class, place of service, rate type) contexts that carry more than one distinct rate
why: Conflicting prices for the same service and provider make the 'true' rate ambiguous and force a selection rule; tolerance 10%

definition: Days between the file's last_updated_on and the as-of date; full score up to 31 days, zero at 365
why: TiC requires monthly refreshes; an old file misstates today's contracts

definition: Share of rate rows whose expiration_date is before the as-of date (9999-12-31 = open-ended)
why: Expired rates are no longer in force and must not be used as current prices; tolerance 10%
